pageDescription: Craft clear, consistent, and user-friendly content in all written communication across the product. Here are some key guidelines:

items.label: Know your audience:
items.text: Write with the audience in mind. Tailor the content to meet the needs, expectations, and understanding of the target users. Avoid overly technical language; keep it visual and intuitive.

items.label: Inclusive language:
items.text: Use inclusive language that avoids bias, stereotypes, and discriminatory phrases.

blocks.label: Friendly yet professional:
items: Keep the tone approachable, but maintain authority.
Write in a way that is encouraging and supportive.

blocks.label: Empowering:
items: Use language that instills confidence in users.
Provide helpful tips and highlight common pitfalls.

blocks.label: Clarity:
blocks.text: Use clear and simple language that's easy to understand. Avoid jargon, technical terms, or complex words when simpler alternatives are available.

blocks.label: Consistency:
blocks.intro: Establish a style guide for terminology, tone and formatting.
items: Use consistent terminology throughout the product. If you refer to something as a "profile" in one place, don't call it an "account" elsewhere.
Maintain a consistent tone and voice across all platforms. Ensure that all content reflects the same friendly yet professional tone, whether it's in a button label or an announcement.

items.text: Standardise punctuation, capitalisation, and formatting rules. Refer

blocks.label: Active Voice:
blocks.text: Prefer active voice over passive voice to make content more direct and engaging (e.g., "Complete the form" instead of "The form should be completed").

blocks.label: Error Messages:
items: Clear and helpful: Error messages should clearly explain what went wrong and how the user can fix it. Avoid technical jargon and be specific about the problem.
Positive tone: Maintain a helpful, non-blaming tone. For example, "Please enter a valid email address" instead of "Invalid email address."

blocks.label: Microcopy:
items: Button labels: Use concise and descriptive text for buttons. Users should understand what will happen when they click a button.
Form labels and instructions: Ensure form labels are clear and concise. Provide guidance where necessary (e.g., placeholder text, tooltips).

blocks.label: Content Hierarchy:
items: Headings and subheadings: Use a clear hierarchy of headings and subheadings to organise content and make it easier to scan.
Bullet points and numbered lists: Use lists to break down complex information into easily digestible parts.

blocks.label: Collaborate:
items: Work closely with business users to ensure accuracy.

blocks.label: Test for Usability:
items: Conduct usability testing with actual users of the application.
Revise content based on feedback and testing outcomes.
